comments.text: Thank you for this absolutely fascinating history of the salt pans, slave entrepot, slave uprising and the story of the liqueur. I had no knowlege of the refinery, its crucial importance in WWII, and the aborted threat to it by Nazi subs. The main thing Curacao always has had, while nothing else has remained the same over time, is its outstanding sheltered deep-water port.  Peter Stuyvesant was the acting governor of Curacao (the main Dutch naval base in the West Indies), Aruba and Bonaire from 1638 to 1644. In 1644 he attacked Sint Maarten (St Martin, which the Spanish had taken from the Dutch) to take it back and had his right leg shattered, requiring amputation and the wearing of a wooden leg. The next year he was appointed Director-General of Nieuw Nederland Kolonie, whose capital was Nieuw Amsterdam. Stuyvesant turned over Nieuw Amsterdam to the invading English in 1664, who changed its name to New York.
